intro: Simpson integration fits local quadratics over pairs of equal-width intervals. The alternating weights arise from adding those local integrals while shared interior endpoints appear twice.
task: Validate odd sample count and apply alternating interior weights to a fixed-spacing sample vector.
requirements: values is an odd-length vector of 3..63 evenly spaced function samples. spacing is in [1e-6,10000].
Return spacing/3 times the weighted sum with endpoint weights 1, odd interior weights 4 and even interior weights 2.
Samples may be negative. This is signed area; do not take absolute values.

Unless a requirement explicitly sets another range, numeric inputs are real and finite with magnitude at most 10000. Booleans are rejected except explicit boolean masks. Vectors have length 1..64 and matrix axes 1..64 unless specified otherwise. Leave inputs unchanged. Raise ValueError for invalid types, bounds, shapes or documented domain conditions.

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Use separate slices for odd and even interior sample indices.

hints.title: Build the result
hints.body: Apply endpoint weights only once, then multiply the entire weighted sum by spacing/3.

explanation: Simpson integration fits local quadratics over pairs of equal-width intervals. The alternating weights arise from adding those local integrals while shared interior endpoints appear twice.
Odd sample count means an even number of intervals. For constant, linear, quadratic and cubic polynomials the rule is exact apart from rounding, giving strong independent checks.
